rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They argue that if God misleads as Satan does, God deserves blame and refuge; Satan’s lack of causal power would shift all responsibility for misguidance to God.
rows.anchor: قالوا بل خصيصية الله تعالى في ذلك أكثر إذ تضليل إبليس سواء وجوده وعدمه فيما يرجع إلى حصول الضلال

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They argue that God attributes misguidance to Pharaoh, the Samaritan, people, and Satan; if God alone caused it, blaming them is false, and shared causation makes their blame unjust.
rows.anchor: وسادسها : أنه تعالى أضاف الإضلال عن الدين إلى غيره وذمهم لأجل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī frames 2:28–40 as an account of four blessings common to all accountable people; life is the first, before the blessings of earth and sky.
rows.anchor: من هذا الموضع إلى قوله : { خالدون يابنى إسراءيل اذكروا نعمتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative “How can you disbelieve?” is a rebuke, since the greater a benefaction, the graver the recipient’s disobedience; God recalls His immense gifts to deter disbelief and prompt faith.
rows.anchor: وإن كان بصورة الاستخبار فالمراد به التبكيت والتعنيف ، لأن عظم النعمة يقتضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life is the foundational blessing and the passage’s central point; Rāzī compares the obligation owed to a benefactor with a child’s greater duty to a nurturing parent.
rows.anchor: فذكر تعالى من نعمه ما هو الأصل في النعم وهو الأحياء ، فهذا هو المقصود الكلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first transition uses fa because life may follow death without delay; thumma marks the delay between life and death and, if resurrection is meant, between death and renewed life.
rows.anchor: لأن الأحياء الأول قد يعقب الموت بغير تراخ ، وأما الموت فقد تراخى عن الأحياء

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites argue that if God creates unbelief, reproaching people for it is as incoherent as reproaching them for God-created color or illness.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : هذه الآية تدل على أن الكفر من قبل العباد من وجوه :

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They argue that if God created people destined for misery and Hell and intended their unbelief, He could not coherently rebuke them for disbelieving.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : هذه الآية تدل على أن الكفر من قبل العباد من وجوه :

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They argue that God cannot demand belief while creating unbelief and blocking faith; such address would be mockery rather than proof against people.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : هذه الآية تدل على أن الكفر من قبل العباد من وجوه :

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They list foreknowledge, divine will, creation of unbelief, and created capacities and volitions as six causes of unbelief, with six corresponding causes of faith absent, making belief impossible.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : هذه الآية تدل على أن الكفر من قبل العباد من وجوه :

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They argue that under compulsion life is no benefaction if God intends to lead an unbeliever to eternal Hell, just as poisoned food is not a gift despite its pleasant appearance.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : هذه الآية تدل على أن الكفر من قبل العباد من وجوه :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī answers that the objections rely on praise, blame, commands, and punishment; divine foreknowledge makes an act contrary to what God knows impossible without making the rebuke incoherent.
rows.anchor: فنحن أيضا نقابلها بالكلام المعتمد في هذه الشبهة ، وهو أن الله سبحانه وتعالى علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He adds that a capacity suited to either belief or unbelief needs a determinant; if the servant supplies it the regress returns, while a divine determinant makes the act necessary.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فالقدرة على الكفر إن كانت صالحة للإيمان امتنع كونها مصدرا للإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All agree that “you were dead” refers to being earth and semen: Adam began from earth, and the other accountable descendants, except Jesus, from semen.
rows.anchor: اتفقوا على أن قوله : { وكنتم أمواتا } المراد به وكنتم ترابا ونطفا

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most scholars say applying “dead” to inanimate matter is figurative: a dead being has undergone death and normally was capable of life, unlike inert matter.
rows.anchor: والأكثرون على أنه مجاز لأنه شبه الموات بالميت وليس أحدهما من الآخر بسبيل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda takes “dead” literally: people were dead in their fathers’ loins, God enlivened and brought them forth, then caused their necessary death and raised them; this yields two lives and two deaths.
rows.anchor: وهو مروي عن قتادة ، قال كانوا أمواتا في أصلاب آبائهم فأحياهم الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī prefers the figurative reading: Arabic calls inert matter mawāt, not mayyit, and mayyit ordinarily implies something that could have lived.
rows.anchor: والأول هو الأقرب ، لأنه يقال في الجماد إنه موات وليس بميت

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffāl compares the phrase to 76:1: humans were nothing remembered, with “dead” used figuratively for something obscure or without a mention.
rows.anchor: قال القفال : وهو كقوله تعالى : { هل أتى على الإنسان حين من الدهر لم يكن شيئا مذكورا }

rows.speaker: المخبل السعدي
rows.claim: Al-Mukhabbal al-Saʿdī’s line illustrates metaphorical life and death of remembrance: some memories remain dormant, while others are more vivid.
rows.anchor: قال المخبل السعدي : فوأحييت لي ذكرى وما خاملا … ولكن بعض الذكر أنبه من بعض …

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some argue that the verse allows only earthly life and resurrection, with two deaths and two lives, so it excludes an intermediate life and punishment in the grave.
rows.anchor: احتج قوم بهذه الآية على بطلان عذاب القبر ، قالوا لأنه تعالى بين أنه يحييهم مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī replies that omission of grave life does not prove its absence; indeed, “then you return to Him” may follow a distinct, non-eternal life in the grave.
rows.anchor: لم يلزم من عدم الذكر في هذه الآية أن لا تكون حاصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed appeal to 40:11 is disputed because it is speech by the disbelievers; a pre-world life of the progeny in Adam could already supply two lives and deaths without grave life.
rows.anchor: لأنه قول الكفار ، ولأن كثيرا من الناس أثبتوا حياة الذر في حلب آدم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the address concerns people generally; some individuals, however, experienced three deaths and revivals in exceptional events.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن رحمه الله قوله : { كيف تكفرون بالله } يعني به العامة ، وأما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī cites the man at the ruined town, those fleeing death, the Israelites struck by lightning, the slain man revived by the cow, and the sleepers of the cave as exceptional cases.
rows.anchor: وأما بعض الناس فقد أماتهم ثلاث مرات نحو ما حكى في قوله

rows.speaker: المجسمة
rows.claim: Corporealists take “you return to Him” to mean that God occupies a place to which people return.
rows.anchor: تمسك المجسمة بقوله تعالى : { ثم إليه ترجعون } على أنه تعالى في مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says the return is to God’s judgment and exclusive authority: He raises the dead and gathers them, as when one says that a matter returns to the prince.
rows.anchor: والمراد أنهم إلى حكمه يرجعون لأنه تعالى يبعث من في القبور ويجمعهم في المحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse proves that only God can give life and death, refuting natural philosophers who assign these effects to stars, elements, or temperaments.
rows.anchor: أنها دالة على أنه لا يقدر على الإحياء والإماتة إلا الله تعالى فيبطل به قول أهل الطبائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s first revival of dead matter supplies a rational indication that He can resurrect it again.
rows.anchor: أنها تدل على صحة الحشر النشر مع التنبيه على الدليل العقلي الدال عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The life-and-death sequence also establishes accountability, encouragement, and warning.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أنها تدل على التكليف والترغيب والترهيب .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says the verse indicates both compulsion and human acquisition, referring back to the preceding discussion of divine determination.
rows.anchor: الرابع : أنها دالة على الجبر والقدر كما تقدم بيانه ، الخامس : أنها دالة على وجوب الزهد في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse teaches detachment from worldly life: God develops a person from semen, grants faculties and possessions, then removes them in death and leaves the body forgotten in its grave.
rows.anchor: فبين أنه لا بد من الموت ثم بين أنه لا يترك على هذا الموت

rows.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ الرازي
rows.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh al-Rāzī pictures relatives passing the grave as if they had never known the deceased, illustrating the loneliness of death.
rows.anchor: فيمر أقاربي بحذاء قبري … كأن أقاربي لم يعرفوني

rows.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ الرازي
rows.claim: His prayer imagines the deceased abandoned in the grave and asks God, the source of ancient kindness, for mercy and forgiveness there.
rows.anchor: وقال أيضا : إلهي كأني بنفسي وقد أضجعوها في حفرتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī describes the final return: the trumpet is blown, the dead rise from graves, stand before God, and fall silent in awe.
rows.anchor: يأمر بأن ينفخ في الصور { فصعق من فى * السماوات * ومن فى الارض

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An unnamed supplicant asks God not to turn away from people resurrected frightened, hungry, exposed, burdened by sins, bewildered, and regretful.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إلهنا إذا قمنا من ثرى الأجداث مغبرة رؤوسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the second universal blessing; the order follows human need, since benefit from earth and sky comes only after life.
rows.anchor: هذا هو النعمة الثانية التي عمت المكلفين بأسرهم وما أحسن ما رعى الله سبحانه وتعالى هذا الترتيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī refers back to his explanation of “who created you” in 2:21.
rows.anchor: أما قوله : { خلق } فقد مر تفسيره في قوله : { اعبدوا ربكم الذى خلقكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “For you” indicates benefits for religious and worldly life: bodily well-being and strength for worship, and reflection on created things as evidence.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله : { لكم } فهو يدل على أن المذكور بعد قوله خلق لأجل انتفاعنا في الدين والدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Everything on earth” gathers benefits from animals, plants, minerals, mountains, crafts, and things human reason has devised.
rows.anchor: جميع المنافع ، فمنها ما يتصل بالحيوان والنبات والمعادن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī connects the verse to God’s subjection of what is in the heavens and earth for people.
rows.anchor: كما قال : { وسخر لكم ما فى * السماوات وما في الارض }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence can be read as two grounds for rebuke: God gave life, and He created everything in earth and sky for human benefit.
rows.anchor: فكأنه سبحانه وتعالى قال كيف تكفرون بالله وكنتم أمواتا فأحياكم وكيف تكفرون بالله وقد خلق لكم ما في السموات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation of the earth’s contents also argues against denying resurrection: the One who created them for people is able to restore them.
rows.anchor: أو يقال كيف تكفرون بقدرة الله على الإعادة وقد أحياكم بعد موتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī points to other passages detailing these benefits, including the pouring of rain and the creation of livestock.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى ذكر تفاصيل هذه المنافع في سورة مختلفة كما قال : { أنا صببنا الماء صبا } وقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī’s Ashʿarite position is that God does not act for an end that would perfect Him, since completion through another would imply prior deficiency.
rows.anchor: قال أصحابنا : إنه سبحانه وتعالى لا يفعل فعلا لغرض لأنه لو كان كذلك كان مستكملا بذلك الغرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If an act’s goal benefits another, that benefit either is preferable to God’s own benefit, implying He gains from it, or is not preferable, leaving no motive to secure it.
rows.anchor: فإن كان أولى فهو تعالى قد انتفع بذلك الفعل فيعود المحذور المذكور وإن كان الثاني لم يكن تحصيل ذلك الغرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Acting for a goal would imply inability to attain it except through that act, which is impossible for God.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : أن من فعل فعلا لغرض كان عاجزا عن تحصيل ذلك الغرض إلا بواسطة ذلك الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the goal were eternal, the act would be eternal; if created, God would make it for another goal, producing an impossible infinite regress.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : أنه تعالى لو فعل فعلا لغرض لكان ذلك الغرض إن كان قديما لزم قدم الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If divine action depended on serving human welfare, God would not impose a harmful burden on those He knows will not believe, yet He does.
rows.anchor: ورابعها : أنه تعالى لو كان يفعل لغرض لكان ذلك الغرض هو رعاية مصلحة المكلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī explains purpose-language in “for you” and “except to worship Me” analogically: God does what would count as goal-directed if another did it.
rows.anchor: أطلق الله عليه لفظ الغرض بسبب هذه المشابهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse implies that God is not needy; if He needed these things, He would have created them for Himself as well as for others.
rows.anchor: قوله : { خلق لكم ما فى الأرض جميعا } يقتضي أنه لا تصح الحاجة على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أهل الإباحة
rows.claim: The permissivists infer that because God created everything on earth for everyone, no one can have an exclusive claim to anything.
rows.anchor: احتج أهل الإباحة بقوله تعالى : { خلق لكم ما فى الأرض جميعا } على أنه تعالى خلق الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects that inference: the collective wording pairs the whole with the whole and individuals with individuals, while separate evidence determines ownership.
rows.anchor: وهو ضعيف لأنه تعالى قابل الكل بالكل ، فيقتضي مقابلة الفرد بالفرد ، والتعيين يستفاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists use the verse to establish that the default rule for benefits is permissibility.
rows.anchor: والفقهاء رحمهم الله استدلوا به على أن الأصل في المنافع الإباحة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some infer that eating clay is forbidden because God created what is in the earth for people, not the earth itself.
rows.anchor: قيل إنها تدل على حرمة أكل الطين لأنه تعالى خلق لنا ما في الأرض دون نفس الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī answers that things located within the earth include minerals and its veins, and mention of one thing does not exclude what is unmentioned.
rows.anchor: وكذلك عروق الأرض وما يجري مجرى بعض لها ولأن تخصيص الشيء بالذكر لا يدل على نفي الحكم عما عداه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istiwāʾ can mean standing upright or straightening, but that bodily sense cannot apply to God.
rows.anchor: الاستواء في كلام العرب قد يكون بمعنى الانتصاب وضده الإعوجاج ولما كان ذلك من صفات الأجسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects spatial elevation: it would already exist before earth’s creation, contradicting thumma, which marks a later sequence here.
rows.anchor: ولو كان المراد من هذا الاستواء العلو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He interprets the phrase as turning directly toward or intending the sky, like a straight arrow aimed without distraction, and creating it after earth.
rows.anchor: استوى إليه كالسهم المرسل إذا قصده قصدا مستويا من غير أن يلتفت إلى شيء آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī reads 41:9–10 as two days for earth, two more for its provisions, then two for heaven, totaling the six days mentioned elsewhere.
rows.anchor: مفسر بقوله : { قل * أئنكم * لتكفرون بالذي خلق الأرض في يومين وتجعلون له

rows.speaker: بعض الملحدة
rows.claim: Some critics see a chronology conflict: 2:29 and 41:9–10 place earth before heaven, while 79:27–30 appears to place earth after heaven.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الملحدة هذه الآية تدل على أن خلق الأرض قبل خلق السماء وكذا قوله

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: One scholarly answer distinguishes creating earth from spreading it: earth was created first, then spread after the sky was made.
rows.anchor: أحدها : يجوز أن يكون خلق الأرض قبل خلق السماء إلا أنه ما دحاها حتى خلق السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī objects that earth’s physical body cannot be separated from its spreading, and that creating everything in it before heaven requires it already to have been spread.
rows.anchor: أن الأرض جسم عظيم فامتنع انفكاك خلقها عن التدحية وإذا كانت التدحية متأخرة عن خلق السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reply says 79:30 delays only earth’s spreading, not its creation, until after the sky’s creation.
rows.anchor: والجواب : أن قوله تعالى : { والأرض بعد ذلك دحاها } يقتضي تقديم خلق السماء على الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī responds that 79:27–30 places the sky’s creation and leveling before earth’s spreading; if spreading accompanies earth’s substance, the difficulty returns.
rows.anchor: ولقائل أن يقول : قوله تعالى : { أشد خلقا أم السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī’s preferred solution is that thumma enumerates blessings rather than chronology, so what is mentioned later may have occurred earlier.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : وهو الجواب الصحيح أن قوله : ( ثم ) ليس للترتيب ههنا وإنما هو على جهة تعديد النعم
